summary:
The Monkey D. Luffy borderless manga art numbered OP09-119 comes from the Emperors in the New World block, a title pointing at the Four Emperors - the small group of pirates whose power defines the second half of the Grand Line and whose presence marks the story's escalation into its late stages. The borderless treatment is the detail that distinguishes this card technically. Removing the frame lets the artwork run to the edge of the stock, which turns the card into an uninterrupted image and, in the process, removes the visual buffer that normally disguises centering problems. It is the most display-oriented format in the range and the least forgiving one to print.

### Basic Info
*   **Main subject / card theme:** Monkey D. Luffy, captain of the Straw Hat Pirates
*   **Set or product (catalog label):** 2024 Emperors In the New World (Op09) - English (Borderless, Manga Art) Alt Art
*   **Card number:** OP09-119
*   **Language version(s):** English printing, per the catalog label
*   **Rarity / treatment:** Borderless manga art alternate art
*   **Set label year:** 2024

### Community Pulse
Borderless cards generate the sharpest condition discussion in One Piece collecting, and this one is a standard example of why. With no frame to absorb the eye, any centering drift is immediately obvious, and edge whitening reads as damage to the artwork itself rather than as wear on a border. Collectors consequently treat borderless printings as high-variance grading submissions - the ceiling is a spectacular card, the floor is a copy that looks visibly wrong even at mid grade. The combination with manga-art linework compounds it, since a monochrome field also advertises print lines. Alongside the technical talk, the block title carries weight: the Four Emperors arc material is among the most collected in the franchise, and cards drawn from that period attract buyers who follow the story rather than the game. Identification questions are routine, given how many treatments share the 119 slot convention across blocks.

### Card Fun Facts
*   Borderless printing removes the frame that normally hides centering error, which is why these cards are simultaneously the most attractive and the riskiest to submit for grading.
*   The Four Emperors are the power structure that defines One Piece's New World, so a block named after them draws on some of the franchise's highest-stakes material.
*   Stacking two demanding treatments - borderless and monochrome manga art - on one card produces a surface where essentially nothing can be concealed.

### Summary (TLDR)
OP09-119 borderless manga-art Luffy pairs the game's most display-forward format with its most exposing art style, under the 2024 Emperors in the New World English label. The absence of a border makes centering and edge condition immediately visible, which turns grading into a high-variance decision and makes clean copies disproportionately prized.
